| [THEORY-020](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-020.md) | Every Boolean algebra is the clopen algebra of its Stone space of prime ideals, and a finite one is the power set of its atoms, so a single Boolean context always has two-valued valuations and the Kochen–Specker obstruction lies in how contexts overlap | Stone (1936, 1937), [LIT-353](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-353.md) and [LIT-358](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-358.md): every Boolean ring is isomorphic to the compact open sets of its prime-ideal space, a totally disconnected, locally compact Hausdorff space that is compact exactly when there is a unit, and every such space arises this way. | [THEORY-168](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-168.md) v2 | In Contextuality-by-Default, whether a fixed set of measurements is contextual depends on how the system is represented: which couplings are imposed, and which dichotomizations of the variables are included | Dzhafarov, Cervantes & Kujala (2017), [LIT-790](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-790.md), with Dzhafarov & Kujala's CbD 2.0 ([LIT-831](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-831.md)) and CbD 1.0 ([LIT-777](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-777.md)). With every dichotomization kept, two content-sharing variables are contextual on their own unless one nominally dominates the other. The authors present the representation as the analyst's choice, not as a defect. What the record does not get from these papers is any rule for choosing it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-171](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-171.md) v3 | When the causal constraints on events depend on context, deterministic assignments that are causal in each context can fail to glue into one causal assignment, so causal structure is itself a source of contextuality | From Gogioso & Pinzani's trilogy: The Topology of Causality, [LIT-808](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-808.md), read in [NOTE-612](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-612.md), with the definitions of The Combinatorics of Causality, [LIT-800](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-800.md) ([NOTE-635](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-635.md)). | [THEORY-174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md) v2 | Classical simulations between empirical models on different scenarios never create contextuality, and a map between model sets is such a simulation exactly when a non-contextual model of the hom scenario induces it | Karvonen (2018), [LIT-846](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-846.md); Abramsky, Barbosa, Karvonen & Mansfield (2019), [LIT-847](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-847.md); Barbosa, Karvonen & Mansfield (2021, v2 2024), [LIT-845](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-845.md). | [THEORY-231](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-231.md) v3 | Within classical realism, a generalized-noncontextuality no-go refutes Leibnizian representations, not realist representations as such; it rests on a stronger assumption than a Bell-like no-go and so applies where none exists, as in prepare-measure scenarios, but only Leibnizianity implying noncontextuality is proved | Schmid, Selby and Spekkens (2020), [LIT-945](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-945.md), §VI.C, §VIII (Eqs. 200, 214, 215), read in part in [NOTE-737](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-737.md), which is Skimmed: §§II–IV and the proofs in Appendices C–G were not read. Both readings recomputed the criteria. That 71.1% CbD-contextual measures BERT's uncertainty is [NOTE-648](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-648.md)'s derivation from the stipulated support (CNT1 = 2 − Δ). The only possibilistically contextual phrase model has hand-set supports. Neither study uses human judgements, so neither bears on whether people's interpretations are contextual. | Active |
| [THEORY-720](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-720.md) | Classical simulations between no-signalling empirical models on finite scenarios, which may change the cover, never create contextuality: a model is non-contextual exactly when the empty model simulates it, the non-contextual fraction cannot fall along a simulation, strong contextuality is reflected backwards, and only non-contextual models can be cloned | Karvonen (2018), [LIT-846](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-846.md), Theorems 4.1, 4.3 and 4.5, read in [NOTE-651](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-651.md); Abramsky, Barbosa, Karvonen & Mansfield (2019), [LIT-847](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-847.md), Theorems 21 and 22, read in [NOTE-647](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-647.md). A classical simulation answers each measurement of the target by a jointly measurable set of the source's, with shared classical randomness, so the cover may change. Non-contextual models are exactly those the empty model simulates, NCF cannot fall along a simulation, strong contextuality is reflected backwards, and a model clones itself only if it is non-contextual. No-signalling models on finite scenarios only. Which maps are simulations is [THEORY-174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md)'s open half. | Active |
| [THEORY-722](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-722.md) | In Contextuality-by-Default 2.0, whether a system of non-binary variables is contextual depends on which variables represent the measurements: coarse-graining can turn a noncontextual system into a contextual one, while for connections of two variables, and for consistently connected systems, CbD 1.0 and 2.0 agree | Dzhafarov & Kujala (2017), [LIT-831](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-831.md), Examples 1–3 and Section 4, read in [NOTE-643](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-643.md) (claims C4 and C6). Under multimaximal couplings, lumping values of non-binary variables can destroy every multimaximal coupling, so a noncontextual system becomes contextual. The verdict on a fixed set of measurements therefore depends on which variables represent them. For connections of two variables, hence cyclic systems, and for consistently connected systems, the 1.0 and 2.0 definitions agree. It does not say the coupling choice changes verdicts in larger connections, which is [THEORY-168](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-168.md)'s asserted part. | Active |
